book: The Didache — The Teaching of the Twelve

1: There are two ways, one of life and one of death, and there is a great difference between the two ways. The way of life is this: first, you shall love God who made you; second, your neighbour as yourself; and all things whatsoever you would not have done to you, do not do to another.

Bless those who curse you, and pray for your enemies; fast for those who persecute you. For what credit is it if you love those who love you? Do not even the heathen do the same? But love those who hate you, and you shall not have an enemy.

My child, flee from every evil thing, and from everything that resembles it. Do not be angry, for anger leads to murder; do not be jealous, nor quarrelsome, nor hot-tempered, for from all these murder is born. Be meek, for the meek shall inherit the earth — and the earth is already being divided among them.
2: You shall not murder a child by abortion, nor kill one that is born. You shall not covet your neighbour's goods; you shall not take away your neighbour's livelihood; you shall not plot evil against your neighbour.

You shall not turn away the needy, but shall share everything with your brother, and shall not say that anything is your own — for if you are sharers in what is immortal, how much more in what is mortal?

My child, do not be a liar, for lying leads to theft; do not be avaricious, nor vain-glorious, for from all these thefts are born. Do not be a murmurer, for murmuring leads to blasphemy; do not be self-willed, nor evil-minded, for from all these blasphemies are born. But be meek, since the meek shall inherit the earth.
3: My child, day and night remember him who speaks the word of God to you, and honour him as the Lord — for where the Lordship is spoken of, there the Lord is. And seek out daily the faces of the saints, that you may be refreshed by their words.
[Didache 4:9-10 — Do not be one who stretches out]

Do not be one who stretches out his hands to receive, and draws them in when he should give. If you have something through your hands, give a ransom for your sins. Do not hesitate to give, nor grumble when you give — for you will know who is the good Paymaster of the reward.

Watch for your life; let your lamps not be quenched and your loins not ungirded, but be ready — for you know not the hour in which our Lord comes. Gather yourselves often, seeking the things that befit your souls; for the whole time of your faith will not profit you if you are not perfected in the last time.
